graph.name: US B1/B2 Visa Process — Brazilian Professor, Short-Term Academic Visit
graph.description: End-to-end B1/B2 application route for a Brazilian professor invited to the United States for a short academic exchange (seminars, lectures, laboratory visits). Covers the 9-5-6 honorarium rule, the B1-versus-J1 boundary, the two available application venues (Brazil or Guangzhou, China), the document set, the interview, and post-approval steps through EVUS and entry.

notes.dec-loc:
Two venues are available, and each carries a different evidentiary burden and a different wait time.
- Venue A - Brazil: apply in Sao Paulo or Rio de Janeiro; the strongest case, because the tenured post and the family ties are local and easy to document
- Venue B - Guangzhou, China: permitted only when the professor is physically in China holding a valid Chinese residence permit
- Trade-off on speed: Guangzhou schedules faster, but the officer then weighs the ties to China, which can be thinner than the ties to Brazil
- Trade-off on waiting: Sao Paulo and Rio are heavily booked, typical waits run 1 to 3 months
- If Guangzhou is chosen, the residence permit, the local appointment and the local address all have to be documented
- The choice fixes the DS-160 consulate selection, the fee payment channel and the passport return option, so it precedes every other step
- Recommendation for a Brazil-based professor: apply in Brazil unless the return timeline is genuinely tight
- Reversing the choice later is not free: it means a fresh DS-160 and a fresh fee at the new consulate
notes.dec-outcome:
The decision is delivered at the window on the day of the interview.
- Approved: the passport is retained for visa printing, and the officer may state the visa validity verbally
- Refused under 214(b): the passport is handed back on the spot together with a refusal sheet
- Administrative processing: the passport may be held and the case leaves the window undecided; this is neither approval nor refusal
- The refusal sheet names the section applied, so it must be read before leaving the building - it is not reissued
- Under administrative processing a 221(g) sheet lists what to submit and by when; missing that deadline closes the file
- Visa validity is not the length of stay; the officer decides the visa, and the border officer decides the period of admission
- Record which outcome occurred and the date, because it governs both the next step and any future reapplication
notes.doc-cv:
The English CV establishes that the professor is a genuine academic with a position to return to.
- Front-load: current institution, department, academic rank and years in post
- Research direction in two or three lines, in the vocabulary of the host field, so the match is visible
- Publication list: selected recent outputs with venue names; the full list is not required
- Funding and awards: grants held, especially any that continue after the trip - evidence that the professor returns to work
- Prior international collaborations and prior compliant travel, if any
- Home address and contact details, consistent with the employment letter
- Keep it identical to the CV described in the DS-160; discrepancies invite questions at the window
notes.doc-employment:
The employment letter is the primary counter to 214(b): it shows a secure post that requires the professor to come back.
- Issued by the home university on letterhead, in English, signed and stamped
- Must state: the professor holds a current teaching or research appointment, the rank, and the start date
- Must state: the university approves leave for the specific dates of the US visit
- Must state: the professor is expected back on duty on a named date, and the post continues on return
- A salary statement is useful: it shows the professor is paid at home and therefore has no reason to work in the United States
- Dates must be consistent with the invitation letter and the DS-160 itinerary
- If the professor is Brazilian but applying in Guangzhou, add proof of the Chinese residence permit and of the appointment held in China
notes.doc-invite:
The invitation letter is the core academic evidence, and its wording decides whether the case is B1-clean.
- Format: host university letterhead, signed by the host; a scan printed in colour is accepted at the interview
- Required content: professor full name as printed in the passport, and the passport number
- Required content: the exact visit dates, start and end
- Required content: the academic activities - seminars, lectures, discussions with faculty, laboratory visits
- Required content: who bears which cost
- When no honorarium is offered, the letter must state that no salary or employment compensation is provided and that only reasonable travel and accommodation expenses are reimbursed
- When an honorarium is offered, the letter must state the total duration and confirm that it does not exceed 9 days
- Host contact block: name, title, department, email and phone, so the officer can verify the invitation
- Weak letters are a leading cause of 214(b) refusals: a vague purpose plus vague funding reads as a work trip
notes.doc-passport:
Passport validity is a hard gate: it must extend at least 6 months beyond the intended departure from the United States.
- Rule: valid 6 months beyond the date of departure from the United States, not merely beyond the date of entry
- Rule: at least one fully blank page for the visa foil
- Bring the previous passport as well if it carries earlier US visas or entry stamps - prior compliant travel helps the case
- Brazilian passports are normally valid 10 years, so renewal is rarely needed, but the expiry must be checked against the planned departure
- Name spelling in the passport has to match the DS-160 exactly, including accents and middle names
- Checked at the ASC and again at the interview window; a shortfall costs the appointment
- Photocopy the identity pages and keep the copy in the interview folder
notes.doc-ties:
Financial and family evidence exists to rebut 214(b), the presumption that every applicant intends to immigrate.
- Bank statements covering the last 3 months, showing funds sufficient for the trip
- Even when the host reimburses travel, the statements matter: they show independent capacity
- Property, lease or mortgage documents for the residence the professor returns to
- Family documents: spouse and children, and where they live
- Employment continuity evidence: contract, tenure or appointment letter
- Ongoing grants or student supervision that cannot be abandoned
- Bring originals plus one photocopy set; the officer typically inspects rather than keeps
notes.end-entry:
Entry is granted by the CBP officer at the port of entry, not by the visa itself.
- Carry in hand luggage: passport with visa, invitation letter, employment letter, return itinerary, EVUS confirmation
- Expect the questions: purpose of the visit, intended duration, where the professor will stay, and who pays
- Typical admission on B1/B2 is up to 6 months, but the officer decides and records the exact date in the I-94
- Check the I-94 record online after arrival; the admitted-until date is what governs the stay
- Keep the I-94 printout with the travel documents for the whole stay, since it is the only record of that date
- Secondary inspection is possible; stay factual, hand over the invitation letter, and do not raise employment topics unprompted
- Do not take US wages or engage in research that the host directs - that breaches the B1 terms and the admission
- Depart before the admitted-until date; an overstay voids the visa and future eligibility
notes.out-refusal:
A 214(b) refusal is not appealable; the only route forward is a new application with a materially stronger case.
- Meaning: the officer was not satisfied that the professor has a residence abroad that will be returned to
- There is no appeal and no reconsideration of the same file; a new DS-160 and a new fee are required
- What actually changes the outcome: a tighter employment letter with a return date, clearer financial evidence, concrete family and property ties, and a crisper invitation stating academic purpose and duration
- Common triggers: a vague invitation, a visit that looks like work, gaps in the employment documentation, or answers that contradict the papers
- Do not reapply with the same paperwork - the second officer sees the first refusal on the record
- Reapply only after the specific weakness has been changed; an essentially identical file is refused again
- A refusal does not affect a different visa category later, and it does not cancel a visa that is still valid
- A refusal does not bar future travel; a materially improved case can succeed
notes.rule-956:
The 9-5-6 rule: an honorarium is allowed only for a visit of 9 days or less, and only from a limited number of US institutions.
- Condition 1 - duration: the visit during which the honorarium is paid must not exceed 9 days
- Condition 2 - frequency: no more than 5 US institutions may have paid a like honorarium in the past 6 months
- Condition 3 - nature of payment: an honorarium for a lecture or seminar is acceptable; wages or research stipends are not
- Travel and accommodation reimbursement is always allowed and is not an honorarium
- The two numeric limits, written out:
$$d \le 9 \qquad \text{and} \qquad n_{\text{inst}} \le 5$$
- Practical consequence: if the visit runs longer than 9 days the host must either drop the honorarium, or the professor needs a different category entirely
- Because the invitation letter must state the duration, this rule has to be settled before the letter is written
notes.rule-cat:
B1 covers short academic exchange; J1 is required as soon as the visit becomes real research collaboration.
- B1: consultations, seminars, lectures, laboratory visits, conference attendance - no employment relationship
- J1: a substantive joint research project, a visiting-scholar appointment, or any activity the host supervises as work
- The boundary is the deliverable, not the duration: if the professor produces research output for the host under host direction, B1 is the wrong category
- B1 is issued as B1/B2 combined, so one visa also covers tourism around the academic activity
- Cost of getting this wrong: a B1 used for J1 activity is a status violation and can bar future entry
- Decision inputs: the invitation wording, whether the host pays a salary or a stipend, and whether a joint project is named
- Practical test: if the host would need to issue an appointment letter, it is J1
notes.rule-pay:
B1 forbids any salary, wage or research stipend from the US host - only travel cost reimbursement is safe.
- Allowed: airfare, accommodation, local travel costs, and an honorarium that stays inside the 9-5-6 limits
- Forbidden: a salary, an hourly wage, a stipend for research work, or payment for producing a deliverable
- Forbidden in substance even when not labelled as salary: any payment tied to work that the host directs
- The professor keeps being paid by the home institution - that is what keeps the B1 status clean
- Interview risk: the officer asks directly whether any payment will be received; answer precisely and separate reimbursement from honorarium
- If the host insists on paying for research work, switch to J1 before filing - do not file B1 and hope
- Written evidence: when no honorarium is offered, the invitation letter must contain the reimbursement-only sentence
notes.start-visit:
Invitation received from a US host university for a short academic visit.
- Trigger: a US department invites the professor for seminars, lectures or laboratory visits
- Typical duration: a few days to a few weeks; the honorarium variant is capped at 9 days
- Purpose code to keep in mind: B1 business visitor, not employment
- What the host must send: a letter on university letterhead naming the professor, the dates and the activities
- What the professor must confirm before any form is filed: passport validity, prior US visa history, and current immigration status in the country of application
- Next card: the visa category is not automatic - it follows from the payment terms and from whether a joint project exists
notes.step-appt:
Step 3 - the appointment and the biometrics slot are booked, and the wait time becomes the critical path.
- Brazil: two bookings, first the ASC for fingerprints and a photograph, then the consulate interview; Sao Paulo and Rio are heavily booked, 1 to 3 months is typical
- Guangzhou: one consolidated booking, ASC enrolment immediately followed by the consulate interview
- Book the ASC and the interview as close together as the system allows - the ASC record feeds the interview file
- Confirm the passport return option chosen earlier and note the estimated return window
- Print the appointment confirmation letter; it is demanded at both doors
- Only the applicant enters; no accompanying person is admitted
- If no slot exists inside the needed window, watch the service for released cancellations rather than booking in a third country
- The booking sets the date of travel planning, so flight reservations should stay refundable until the interview is done
notes.step-asc:
Step 5a - at the Application Support Center the applicant is fingerprinted and photographed.
- Bring: passport, DS-160 confirmation page, appointment confirmation letter
- Collected: ten-finger electronic fingerprints plus a live photograph
- Purpose: this biometric record is what the consular officer compares at the window
- Arrive at the appointment time, neither early nor late; phones are usually not permitted inside
- The photograph taken here is not the visa photograph - that one was uploaded with the DS-160
- Failure to attend without cancelling forces a fresh booking, and in Brazil that can cost months
- In Guangzhou the ASC step and the interview happen back to back on the same day
notes.step-ds160:
Step 1 - the DS-160 online form is the application itself; every other document only supports it.
- Portal: the Consular Electronic Application Center; one form per applicant
- Visa class: select B1/B2, and select the consulate chosen in the venue decision
- Photograph: 51 x 51 mm, white background, taken within 6 months, no glasses
- Content: Brazilian passport data, academic history, prior US travel, the US itinerary and the host contact
- The honorarium and reimbursement answers must be consistent with the invitation letter
- On submission: save and print the confirmation page with the barcode, and record the Application ID and the security questions
- Prerequisites to have on the desk first: passport, invitation letter, English CV
- The Application ID is required for the next step, so the session must not be closed without it
notes.step-evus:
EVUS enrolment is mandatory before boarding a flight to the United States; without it the airline will refuse carriage.
- Who: holders of a 10-year B1/B2 visa travelling on a passport from a participating country - Brazil included
- When: before every departure, and it must still be valid at the time of travel
- Cost: USD 8; validity: 2 years, or until the passport or the visa expires, whichever comes first
- Portal: the official Electronic Visa Update System; avoid paid third-party lookalike sites
- What is entered: passport data, visa data, employment and US contact details, all consistent with the visa file
- Print the enrolment confirmation and carry it together with the invitation letter
- A pending or unsuccessful enrolment has to be resolved before any non-refundable ticket is bought
notes.step-interview:
Step 5b - the consular interview decides the case, in English or in Portuguese, within a few minutes.
- Only the applicant is admitted; documents are carried in one folder and handed over on request
- Expected questions: purpose of the visit, the host institution, the dates, who pays, and where the professor works now
- The payment question must be answered precisely: separate travel reimbursement from an honorarium, and state that no salary is received
- Expected questions: the current appointment, when the professor returns to duty, and what becomes of the post
- Answers must match the invitation letter, the employment letter and the DS-160; inconsistency is what causes refusals
- In practice only the passport, the invitation letter and the employment letter are read; the rest is evidence on standby
- Documents to keep in the folder: passport, DS-160 confirmation, appointment letter, MRV receipt, invitation letter, CV, employment letter, bank statements, ties evidence
notes.step-mrv:
Step 2b - the MRV fee unlocks scheduling and is never refunded.
- Amount: USD 185, the machine-readable visa fee for a B1/B2 application
- Property: non-refundable and non-transferable, even if the visa is refused or the trip is cancelled
- Validity: the receipt is tied to the applicant and to the chosen consulate; it cannot be moved to another person
- Pay only after the DS-160 has been submitted, because the fee is linked to the profile through that application
- The payment proof must be kept in printed form - it is one of the documents carried into the interview folder
- Scheduling stays locked until the payment clears, so this is the real gate before the appointment
- A later reapplication means paying the fee again in full, and a new DS-160 comes with it
notes.step-ustravel:
Step 2a - the appointment service account links the DS-160 to the fee and to the appointment slot.
- Portal: the consular appointment service; one applicant profile per person
- Bind the DS-160 Application ID to the profile - a mismatch blocks scheduling
- Choose the passport return method: courier delivery, or pickup at a designated branch
- In Brazil the fee is paid through a Brazilian bank; in China the channel is CITIC Bank, online or at a counter
- The profile carries the passport data, the delivery address and the visa class; errors here surface at the interview window
- Keep the account email reachable: the appointment confirmation and any rescheduling arrive there
- Screenshot the appointment summary in addition to printing it, in case the confirmation email is lost
- Do not create two accounts for the same applicant; it corrupts the appointment record and delays the case
notes.step-visa:
Step 6a - the passport comes back with the visa foil, and the timing depends on the venue.
- Brazil: typically 5 to 10 working days after approval
- Guangzhou: typically 3 to 7 working days
- Check the foil immediately: name spelling, passport number, visa class B1/B2, and the expiry date
- If the foil is wrong, do not travel - report it to the issuing consulate for correction before departure
- Brazilian nationals are routinely issued a 10-year multiple-entry B1/B2; visa validity is not the permitted length of stay
- Review the annotation block; an unexpected annotation should be queried before travel is booked
- Note the issue date and expiry in a calendar so the EVUS cycle and any renewal can be planned
- Keep a photocopy of the visa page, and keep the old passport if it carried a previous visa
